thread:
acme_infra: hitting a wave of 502/504s on hosted generate today during our nightly import job. starts ~02:12 UTC and lasts in spikes. sample trace id: trace-7a9c3f-048. getting repeated SDK retries that make it worse. can you look?
elaine_support: sorry about that — we're looking. can you paste the full request headers + approximate qps? any change to prompt size or model? :eyes: 
acme_infra: qps ~120 sustained for 3min bursts, prompt ~18k tokens (long chain of docs). model: redwood/open-instruct-xxl. SDK v1.4.2 with default retries. headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>, User-Agent: acme-importer/2.1
acme_infra: sample gateway response: 
```
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
content-type: application/json
{"error":"upstream timeout","correlation_id":"trace-7a9c3f-048","node":"gw-az1-12"}
```
sam_engineer: thanks. that correlation id maps to a prefix-eviction error in our serving logs (kvcache eviction cascade). sending to SRE now. can you reproduce with a shorter prompt and streaming disabled? sometimes large prefix + synchronous generate trips a locking path.
jen_sre: looping in. saw concurrent session evictions from that customer tenant around 02:11:55. eviction is triggered when KVCACHE entries exceed cap and we try to rehydrate during tokenism. temp hypothesis: long prompts + many concurrent requests cause a hot-kv lock which stalls response threads -> gateway timeouts and client retries cascade.
opsbot: created incident INC-4801234 for support thread. assigned to jen_sre and sam_engineer.
elaine_support: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) ask customer to drop prompt to <8k tokens for bursts, 2) enable streaming so partial tokens return faster, 3) temporarily throttle their integration to 40 qps while we patch. any preference?
acme_infra: we need a repro plan — can we run a local script to simulate what they hit?
sam_engineer: repro script (run from a dev box, will simulate 100 concurrent connections over 2min):
```
for i in $(seq 1 100); do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"redwood/open-instruct-xxl","input":"<18k_token_blob>","stream":false}' &
done
wait
```
jen_sre: also trying a targeted repro that toggles kvcache size to force eviction locally. pushing a staging workload now. will report if we see the same 504s.
billing_bot: noticed increased token billing for acme_infra between 02:10-02:20; flagging for potential double-counting due to client retries.
elaine_support: update for customer now: "We're investigating intermittent 504s for large-batch imports. We've identified a cache-eviction cascade under heavy concurrent long-prompt load and are testing a fix; temporary mitigations: reduce burst qps to 40, shorten prompt length for bursts, or enable streaming. We'll notify once patch deploys."
acme_infra: ok will apply throttling on our end for tonight. appreciate ETA for patch?
sam_engineer: ETA: small config change to avoid aggressive kvcache eviction in serving runtime — aiming to roll to canary in 2 hours, full rollout in 6 hours if canary looks good. will attach repro logs.
jen_sre: canary started on gw-az1-13. early signs: queue depth dropped 30% under synthetic load, no observed 504s in first 10m. continuing validation.
elaine_support: customer notified with temporary steps and we've enabled a service note in their tenant config to auto-throttle if 5xx rate > 1% for 5m. :white_check_mark:
acme_infra: thanks. if you can also share recommended SDK config to avoid retry storms (we have control over backoff), that helps.
sam_engineer: recommended SDK snippet: 
```
clientConfig.retry: {
  maxAttempts: 4,
  baseDelayMs: 200,
  maxDelayMs: 2000,
  jitter: true,
  onlyRetryOn: [429, 500, 502, 503]
}
```
and set streaming=true for big prompts.
jen_sre: final: rolling to full after 30m of successful canary. will close incident once customer confirms stability.
elaine_support: I'll send a post-mortem to the account and follow up on billing flag.
acme_infra: closing loop here — re-run import with throttling and streaming, saw no 504s. will reopen if problem resurfaces. thanks all. :tada:
